author: cam
body: Allocates a 64MB flat buffer via __heap-advance. This must run AFTER all codegen is complete (text-buf/rodata-buf are finalized) or the heap advance will corrupt the codegen workspace.

author: blu
body: `__real_to_text` reads sixty-four bits, so an f32 has to be widened before the call or the helper reads a single-precision bit pattern as double and prints a number nobody computed. This is the same convert `emit-show-real-approx` does for `show`; that path takes an expression and this one takes a value already in RAX, which is why the sequence is written twice rather than shared.

author: blu
body: The scope store is the twin of emit-grant-cap-mask: proc 0's authority to touch the disk is its capability bits, and the extent of that authority is its scope. Both are known at emit time and both are written into the process table before opening runs.

author: blu
body: The value is copied to RAX before RDI is loaded because emit-text-lit allocates its result through the rotating temp pool and may hand back RDI itself; loading the address first would clobber the string pointer with the address it was about to be stored at.

author: blu
body: The opening's scope for a given effect family, which the boot grant hands to proc 0 the same way emit-grant-cap-mask hands it its bits. The manifest pipeline is a List Text of NAMES and drops the scope on the floor (the loader ring) -- but the boot ring does not need the manifest at all: the scope literal is right here in the row at emit time, so it is read straight off the label.

author: blu
body: Two families now have a runtime chokepoint and are carried: the filesystem (a path PREFIX, checked at the three Fat16 gates) and the network (an AUTHORITY, checked at the fetch chokepoint against a runtime URL's host). A console channel is the third relation scope-admits knows about and is NOT carried -- a channel is fixed at compile time by the builtin name and never becomes a runtime value, so there is nothing at runtime to check a stored channel against, and carrying it would be a promise the machine cannot keep.

author: blu
body: The EMPTY STRING is a real answer, not a missing one: an opening that names no scope for the family gets "", the cell holds a valid Text, and the family's relation admits everything by itself (the empty prefix admits every path; an empty authority admits every host). That is what keeps a program which never declared the effect from handing the chokepoint a null pointer.

author: blu
body: Both shapes carry the row, and an opening is usually the second one: `opening : [Console, FileSystem.Read "/config/"] Nothing` is a VALUE with an effect row, not a function, so its type is an EffectfulTy and not a FunTy. EffectfulTy's second field is the scope list, parallel to its name list -- reading the names and ignoring that list is exactly how the scope got dropped everywhere else in this pipeline.

author: blu
body: A program naming BOTH .Read and .Write gets readwrite, which is the union it asked for and not an escalation.

author: blu
body: Both lists are now projections of one table, so a vocabulary name with no cap id cannot be written. A guard whose condition can never hold is not protection, it is furniture; the state it watched for is unreachable, so the walk, the diagnostic and the once-per-compile cost all go with it.

author: blu
body: The boot grant for proc 0 derives from the same manifest names the capability section records: each covered name contributes its kernel capability bits, and anything the manifest does not declare stays ungranted (Concurrent covers task spawn, channels, and process creation -- the three faces of the concurrency authority in this kernel). Identity and Capability are effect-row sources like the rest: a program that declares Identity earns cap-identity at boot, which is what every identity builtin's kernel helper now tests.

author: blu
body: Only the filesystem grant carries one, for the same reason manifest-opening-fs-scope carries only that scope: a path is the one resource string the machine can check. Writing a scope for a family with no runtime chokepoint would be a promise the loader cannot keep.

author: blu
body: The last parameter is the definitions the caller's prune dropped that declared an explicit WCET budget. It is a list and not a chapter because the caller is the only place both the pre-prune and post-prune def lists exist: ir-prune-unreachable-roots stores its result back into the chapter it was given, so a callee holding one chapter cannot recover the other. An empty list is the honest default for a caller that did not prune.
